title: Quarterly Pulse: Dedicated Pool Healthscore, Latency‑Led Autoscale & Rehearsal Playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Purpose: Define a repeatable quarterly playbook that ties dedicated pool capacity decisions to a single healthscore (pool health) and a latency‑led autoscale pulse. The playbook will standardize: 1) an operator-facing healthscore dashboard used in weekly capacity reviews, 2) a canary + rehearsal process for autoscale rule changes, and 3) an economic simulation to decide reservation vs. burst tradeoffs for the quarter.

Scope: Focus on Dedicated pools (reserved GPU capacity) and associated autoscale policies used by enterprise customers. Excludes edge cases for on‑prem/private installations in this quarter (will be handled Q3).

Success metrics: 
- Pool Healthscore improvement: +15% composite (utilization stability, p95 latency headroom, cold start incidence)
- Reduce unplanned overprovision events by 30% quarter over quarter
- Decision confidence: run economic sims for top 5 customers (>=90% variance explained)

Key components: 
1) Healthscore model: composite of utilization variance, p95 request latency vs SLO, KV cache hit rate, and prewarm readiness. Each pool will show a single 0–100 score and contributing submetrics.

2) Latency‑Led Autoscale Pulse: a periodic policy that preferentially prioritizes low-latency routes when triggering fast scale-up and uses conservative scale-down windows controlled by pool healthscore. Pulse runs as part of the autoscale control loop and has explicit rollback thresholds.

3) Rehearsal & Canary Process: a repeatable quarterly rehearsals calendar where we apply autoscale policy changes to a small set of non-sensitive pools (10% weight) for one week, capture regressions, and run traffic‑shaping simulations.

4) Economic Simulation: per-customer model that simulates reservation vs burst economics under demand traces and autoscale pulse behavior to recommend reservation levels and hedging.

Deliverables: playbook doc, healthscore dashboard prototype in Console, automation for canary rollout, economic simulation notebooks, and runbook for incident response tied to healthscore drops.

2026-02-04 — Liam O'Connor: Added rehearsal calendar proposal. Proposal: one-week canaries per quarter with automatic rollback if p95 latency increases >10% OR error rate >2x baseline. Posted PRD to Confluence and tagged for security review if customer data included.
risks: 1) Incomplete observability (KV cache tagging) will bias healthscore and canary outcomes. 2) Incorrect cost inputs could drive poor reservation recommendations. 3) Canary-induced flakiness could temporarily impact downstream SLAs if rollbacks are slow.
decisions: 1) Use a single composite healthscore for operator simplicity, but expose submetrics for root cause. 2) Run canaries only on non-sensitive pools (no customer PII traffic). 3) Default reservation recommendation will favor cost-neutral hedging unless economic sim shows >8% savings.
